quick-start.title: Quick start
quick-start.summary: Get an account, see how CoGA is organised, review a first case, and keep the five rules for safe use in mind.
paragraphs: Choose Sign in with Microsoft and sign in with the Microsoft account of your hospital or university. Your first sign-in makes your CoGA account; you see a project's data once an administrator has given you access to it. Where CoGA runs without Microsoft sign-in, choose Sign up on the sign-in page and fill in Create account instead: you can sign in once an administrator has activated the account and given you access to your projects. Logout signs you out of CoGA; on a shared computer, then choose Sign out of Microsoft on the sign-in page too. The arrow at the right of the top bar opens a menu of the main sections: the projects, the explorers, the gene panels, this guide and, for administrators, Admin. Settings in the same bar holds your display preferences.
CoGA keeps the pedigree, the assay data and your interpretation together, so a case is reviewed as a whole:
To set up a new case, see Case setup and data import.
blocks: A project decides who sees the data and which reference assembly applies. You see only the projects you belong to; administrators see everything and create the projects. In each of your projects you are an analyst, who reads and changes its records, or a reader, who only reads them; a family page says Read-only access (reader) where you are a reader.
A family is the case: related samples with their pedigree, roles and affected status.
A sample carries the assay data: variants, coverage, segments, repeats and more.
Reference data (genes, cytobands, ClinVar, gnomAD, clinical CNVs and more) belongs to an assembly and is shared by all projects on it.
Review state — classifications, tags and notes — is your interpretation, kept per family.

Use CoGA safely. Decision support only. Review every suggestion, ranking and call; CoGA makes no diagnosis. Screening needs confirmation. Confirm an at-risk NIPT or carrier-screening finding with a diagnostic test. Validated scope only. A family marked Not validated for clinical use is outside the validated assembly (GRCh38) and cannot be signed out. Check Sample QC before sign-out: it confirms that the samples are who the pedigree says. Sign-out closes the analysis. It is the analyst's sign-off, not the medical one: the clinical report is drafted and medically signed in the EPD and refers to the signed version. Only people the laboratory authorises sign out; CoGA refuses it to a reader, but does not check which analyst may.
Decision support only. Review every suggestion, ranking and call; CoGA makes no diagnosis.
Screening needs confirmation. Confirm an at-risk NIPT or carrier-screening finding with a diagnostic test.
Validated scope only. A family marked Not validated for clinical use is outside the validated assembly (GRCh38) and cannot be signed out.
Check Sample QC before sign-out: it confirms that the samples are who the pedigree says.

Sign-out closes the analysis. It is the analyst's sign-off, not the medical one: the clinical report is drafted and medically signed in the EPD and refers to the signed version. Only people the laboratory authorises sign out; CoGA refuses it to a reader, but does not check which analyst may.
On the dashboard, search for a project, family or sample, and open the family.
On the family page, pick the analysis that fits the question. A button appears only when the family has that kind of data.
Check Sample QC before you interpret.
Build a shortlist in the variant list before you open the viewers.
Record your interpretation as you go: classification, tags and notes.

Tag the variants to report with Report, check the drafted report, and have someone the laboratory authorises sign out the analysis. The clinical report is then drafted and medically signed in the EPD, referring to that signed version.

Not finding a variant you expect? The Small variants page opens with a default filter: the Phenotype priority preset on the Mendeliome panel (rare, HIGH or MODERATE impact, carried by the affected members). Press Clear all filters before you conclude that a variant is missing. The Variant explorer leaves out imputed calls unless you tick Include imputed variants.
inline: Not finding a variant you expect?

case-setup.title: Case setup and data import
case-setup.summary: Create a family, import a data package, and know what each kind of data unlocks.
paragraphs: Choose the way in that matches how your data arrives.
blocks: Build a new family by hand: add samples, set sex and roles, link parents and couples, and set affected and carrier status. Open to the analysts of a project, who add families to it, and to administrators; uploading a PED file here is for administrators.
An administrator points at a family folder on the CoGA server, lets CoGA write its manifest, validates it, and imports the family with all its data in one job.

Loading data is for administrators: package import, single uploads on the Upload family and sample data page, and replacing an existing family. Editing an existing family's members or structure is for administrators too. Adding, changing and removing HPO terms is for the analysts of the family's project and for administrators.
For a monogenic NIPT case, tick Monogenic NIPT (cfDNA from maternal plasma) in the family builder: see Monogenic NIPT.

Each kind of data switches on part of CoGA: small variants the small-variant page and Sample QC; structural variants the SV page and the variant summary; TRGT calls the repeat page; Paraphase the paralogue page; mitochondrial calls the mtDNA analysis; coverage, segments, APCAD and haplotypes the viewer tracks.

Reference data first. Genes, cytobands, ClinVar and the other annotation layers are loaded per assembly. If a viewer cannot place coordinates or a gene search is empty, check that the reference data for the family's assembly is loaded.
inline: Data import reference (who may do what, reference data, package steps and checks) →

phenotype-matching.title: Phenotypes, panels and phenotype matching
phenotype-matching.summary: Record HPO terms, focus a search with a gene panel, and match the phenotype to genes and diseases with Monarch.
paragraphs: The patient's phenotype drives the ranking. Record it as HPO terms, and use gene panels to focus a search.

HPO terms are kept per person. An analyst of the family's project or an administrator adds them: click the person's sample name on the family page, and under HPO Phenotypes search a term, choose present, absent or unknown, and press Add phenotype; Remove takes one off. Only present terms are used for matching. Each term added, changed or removed is an entry on the family's Clinical audit trail. A package import can bring terms in too; what it adds or changes is an entry per person, naming who ran the import and the package. A reader sees the terms but cannot change them.

The Panel catalog holds reusable gene lists; administrators create them or import them from PanelApp. Choose a panel in the Locations filter of the small-variant or structural-variant page to limit a search to its genes. The Mendeliome — every gene that Monarch says causes a disease or is associated with one — is the default scope of both pages. A gene Monarch links to a disease only as contributing to it or raising its likelihood is not in it. On the small-variant and structural-variant pages and in the variant explorer a panel keeps the variants annotated with one of its genes and those inside one of its regions (PanelApp's regions for the assembly, and each gene's position in the gene reference; a structural variant that overlaps one), whatever its size: the Mendeliome too keeps a variant inside one of its genes whose annotation names another gene.
CoGA uses the Monarch Initiative knowledge graph, which links genes, diseases and HPO phenotypes.
An administrator loads the Monarch data about monthly (Admin → Monarch data). Until it is loaded, the gene profile shows no associations and the ranking has no phenotype signal.
blocks: On the gene profile (gene explorer), Monarch gene–disease associations lists each linked disease with its relationship, source and number of expected phenotypes. Opened from a family, it also says how many the family shows ("3 observed in family").

On the family page, the Phenotype match (Monarch) panel ranks candidate genes when you press Find candidate genes. It sends the HPO terms of every family member, not only the affected ones. Re-run match runs it again on the phenotypes recorded now, for example after you added one.
In the variant list, the Phenotype priority preset ranks variants partly by how well their gene matches the affected members' phenotypes (see Small-variant prioritisation).

Record specific phenotypes. A broad term such as Intellectual disability is linked to over a thousand genes and gives a weak ranking by design. Add the patient's distinctive features — a particular seizure type, a dysmorphic feature, a metabolic finding — and the ranking sharpens.
inline: Phenotype matching with Monarch reference (the graph, the ranking, PP4) →
furtherReading: In-depth referencePhenotype matching with Monarch reference (the graph, the ranking, PP4) →

family-workspace.title: The family page
family-workspace.summary: The case hub: status and assignment, one button per analysis and viewer, the region of interest, and the family members.
paragraphs: Every case starts on its family page.

The family page and every analysis page (small and structural variants, repeat expansions, Paraphase, mtDNA) open with the same header, so you can work on the case and move between analyses from any of them. One line gives the members, the assembly and the projects, then the page's own figures. Status, Assigned to and Reviewed by track the case's workflow; an analyst of the family's project can change them, a reader only sees them. Assigned to and Reviewed by offer the active analysts of the family's projects and the administrators, never a reader. Someone chosen before they became a reader (or left the family's projects) stays shown, marked (not eligible), until you change it. The header also shows the assembly and the projects, and a Not validated for clinical use banner when the family is outside the validated scope. Beside the workflow fields sit the family-level functions: Sample QC (when the family has small variants) and Report (when it has any variant data: small or structural variants, repeat expansions, Paraphase results or mtDNA data).

At the foot of the header, one row of links leads to the family's analyses: Small variants, Structural variants, Repeat expansions, Paraphase, mtDNA analysis and Monogenic NIPT, with Variant summary (of the structural variants) last, at the right end. A link appears only when the family has that kind of data; on an analysis page its own link is marked.

The ROI is the gene or locus the case is about; PGT uses it for the embryo calls. An administrator sets it (Save, Clear). Anyone can click it to open the chromosome view with 1 Mb on each side. In a PGT family, Review ROI markers → opens the marker review.

One row per person: role, parents, partner, Related to, status, HPO terms and a Seq. QC chip with the sequencing QC verdict and mean depth (hover or focus it for the metrics). A passing chip shows the number alone; any other state is a word on the chip: Warning or Fail when a metric crossed its limit, which the tooltip names, and Not run when the sample's QC was not assessed (no limit set for any of its metrics, or no verdict returned), which is never a pass. An embryo whose QC holds only the PGT pipeline's embryo metrics has no depth to show: its chip gives the value of the metric that decided the verdict (Fail ADO 14.2%), or Not run alone. In a PGT family each embryo also shows its derived call (see Haplotype segregation).

Related to names the member through whom a person is related by an unknown degree, such as a PGT index known to be on the mother's side, or both parents. The pedigree draws the link as a dotted arc with a ?. The haplotype track colours that person along the genome when they turn out to be that member's own parent or child (they share one of the member's haplotypes along nearly every chromosome), and a more distant relative around the ROI, where the markers on both sides show the haplotype they share; elsewhere such a relative stays grey.

Only an administrator edits a member: click the sample name to open Family member details, change the fields, press Apply to pending, then Save pending updates on the family page. HPO terms are added and removed in the same dialog, by an analyst of the family's project or an administrator. Affected status and carrier status are separate: an unaffected person can be a carrier. Remove member in the dialog takes the person out of the family at once, after you confirm. Members are added in Admin → Family & sample data.
Further down are the Phenotype match (Monarch) panel and, closed by default, the Analysis pipeline settings recorded at import.
blocks: Curation gives a line each for the small and the structural variants, the repeat loci and the Paraphase regions: how many are reviewed, how many carry notes, and the count per review tag; for the repeat loci and the Paraphase regions also how many carry your classification.
Visualization — Genome view, Chromosome view, Circos plot and IGV viewer.

sample-qc.title: Sample-integrity QC
sample-qc.summary: Check, before you interpret, that the samples are who the pedigree says: swaps, wrong relationships, wrong sex and consanguinity.
paragraphs: Open a family and press Sample QC to check that the samples are who the pedigree says. A swapped tube, a wrong parent, a mislabelled sex or unexpected relatedness quietly invalidates everything downstream, so run it before you interpret. It does not measure contamination. Some results can be a sign of it, among other causes: a high Mendelian-error rate, or heterozygous calls on a man's X that leave his genetic sex indeterminate or female. A pass does not rule contamination out.
The page first works out what kind of case it is and runs only the checks that fit:
blocks: Long-read WGS family — sex, relatedness against the pedigree, Mendelian errors.
Shallow-WGS PGT — embryo sex and parentage (each embryo a child of both parents), Mendelian errors.
Monogenic NIPT — paternity, fetal sex, parent sex and a check of the cfDNA categories.
Carrier couple — sex per partner, and that the two are unrelated.
Overall verdict — the worst of the checks. A check that could not run counts as a warning, never as a pass, and a note names each sample whose sex could not be checked.
Pedigree — each person's symbol carries a ring and a badge: green ✓ pass, amber ! warning, red ✕ fail. A check that could not run counts as a warning here too. Hover a symbol for the reason.

Per-sample table — recorded sex against genetic sex, and the Mendelian-error rate. The genetic sex carries green ✓ when it matches the record, red ✗ when it does not, amber ! when it could not be confirmed and grey ? when it was not checked. Hover a cell for the reason.
Relatedness matrix — each pair's inferred relationship, kinship and IBS0. A pair that contradicts the pedigree, including parents who look related, is outlined: red for a fail, amber for a warning.
NIPT cards — paternity, fetal sex and the category check, for a cfDNA family.

What to do with a warning or a fail. A fail points to a real problem: re-check the sample sheet, the pedigree and the genotypes before you interpret. A warning usually means too little data to decide (few informative sites, a low fetal fraction, a check that could not run); it weakens the analysis but does not invalidate it. A fail, or a check of the pedigree or of a sample's identity that could not run (a NIPT parent's sex, for example), also stops sign-out until someone records a reason.
inline: What to do with a warning or a fail.

small-variant-filtering.title: Small-variant prioritisation
small-variant-filtering.summary: The small-variant page: the default view, the filters and presets, the phenotype-driven ranking, and genes also hit by a structural variant.
paragraphs: The Small variants page is where most candidates are found. The filters take a genome down to a short list; the Phenotype priority preset puts that list in order.
The page opens with the Phenotype priority (Exomiser-style) preset on the Mendeliome panel:

The filters are grouped as on the screen: Phenotype, Structural second hit, Inheritance, Pathogenicity, Annotations (with Canonical only, MANE only and LoF only), In Silico, Frequency, Locations, Exclude and Review and curation. For de novo and dominant, a male's call on chrX or chrY outside the pseudo-autosomal regions (1 or 1/1) counts as one copy. A location entry that cannot be read (for example an end before its start) is named under its field, and nothing is searched until you fix it. A per-sample minimum (GQ, DP, AF or AD alt) that is not a number fails the search, and the message names it.

The annotation filters must all hold on one transcript of the variant: impact and consequence, the transcript, HGVS, Canonical only, MANE only and LoF only, the ClinVar status, the in-silico scores and the frequencies. With MANE only and HIGH impact, a variant whose HIGH-impact transcript is not its MANE transcript is left out. Under In Silico, one of the predictors you set is enough, and a SpliceAI score at its minimum also passes the impact and consequence filter. A SIFT or PolyPhen choice keeps a transcript whose prediction is exactly that one, whatever score VEP wrote after it: deleterious keeps deleterious(0.01) but not deleterious_low_confidence(0.03), which is a choice of its own, and tolerated leaves out tolerated_low_confidence. The gene, the rsID and the excluded ClinVar statuses apply to the variant as a whole: a gene keeps every variant annotated with it, one VEP places just outside the gene (upstream or downstream) too, ranked or not.

A card, a table row and a CSV row describe one transcript of the variant: MANE Select, else the canonical one, else the most severe. The filters may have held on another: deleterious keeps a variant whose MANE transcript SIFT calls tolerated when a second transcript is deleterious, and HIGH or MODERATE impact keeps one that is synonymous on its MANE transcript and missense on another. The card then says Filters met on under its transcript, and the table row under its effect, with the transcript the filters held on and those of its consequence, LoF and in-silico predictions that read otherwise than the row's; the row's own values stay as they are, and the card's transcript list marks that transcript Filters met. The CSV gives it in its last columns, Filter-matched transcript to Filter-matched PolyPhen. The ranking and ACMG classify read the transcript the row describes.

The built-in presets are Phenotype priority, Dominant strict, Dominant relaxed, Expanded carrier screening (couples only: genes where both partners carry a rare (below 1%) high- or moderate-impact variant, and those variants a female partner carries on chrX outside the pseudo-autosomal regions, which put a son at risk on their own; a ClinVar pathogenic or likely pathogenic call overrides the frequency cut-off, so a common founder variant stays in; a partner whose sex is not recorded counts as female; mitochondrial variants are not part of it, as mtDNA passes from the mother alone), Compound het, Recessive hom, Recessive broad, Any affected and ClinVar review. A preset saves the recipe, not the result; save your own to standardise a search. Compound-heterozygous candidates are shown as pairs. Up to 100 matches show as cards, more as a table.

Your saved searches are shared with the monogenic NIPT page. A search saved there can carry filters only the NIPT list applies: an inheritance view such as De novo in the fetus, the maternal/fetal categories, the minimum confidence. This list does not apply them: the page does not send them, shows no chip for them, and names them once under the active filters. De novo in the fetus is not De novo / dominant, which reads the family members' own genotypes.

With Phenotype priority on, a Score column appears and the rows come ranked, best first. The score combines the variant's own evidence (impact and predictors, ClinVar, rarity, fit with the pedigree) with how well its gene matches the affected members' HPO terms. A ✦ marks a gene that matches. Hover the score, or read the card, for the breakdown: Variant, Pathogenicity, Rarity and Phenotype, the compatible inheritance modes and the matched phenotypes.

Why the ranking can be instant. CoGA keeps the ranking once it is computed; a later open shows ⚡ Prioritised ranking served from cache and when it was computed. It is recomputed automatically when anything it depends on changes: the phenotypes, the pedigree, the panel's genes and regions, the filters (including review-tag filters), the family's variant data, or the reference data (the Monarch release, each import of the HPO ontology, gene constraint, and the gene positions a panel or an excluded gene uses). Narrowing from the Mendeliome to a smaller panel is served from the broader ranking, ranked from 1 within the smaller panel, as long as the Mendeliome's genes and regions are the same as when that ranking was computed. A smaller panel that reaches a variant the broader ranking lacks (through a region of its own, such as the position PanelApp gives for a gene), or that keeps one variant of a compound-het pair without the other, is computed for itself instead.
Download CSV exports the list, with Priority and Rank columns when the ranking is on.

A small variant whose gene is also hit by an SV carries an SV badge (for example SV: DEL), with a trans or cis chip when a phase was decided. Also hit by an SV under Structural second hit keeps only these genes. The phase comes from read phasing or from the parents' genotypes, by the same rule as for compound-het pairs; the reference gives the rule. Each SV of the gene gets its own phase, which the badge's explanation lists, and a deletion in trans with the SNV marks the gene effectively biallelic, whatever the other SVs are.
blocks: gnomAD exome, genome and popmax frequency 1% or below, and at most 10 homozygotes and 10 hemizygotes — a ClinVar pathogenic or likely pathogenic record overrides these cut-offs;
ClinVar benign and likely benign left out;
carried (het or hom) by each affected member, with QUAL 20, depth 10, allele fraction 0.2 and 4 alt reads or more.

The default view hides variants. A variant outside the Mendeliome, a common variant, a low-quality call, or a variant an affected member does not carry is not shown. Press Clear all filters before you conclude that a variant is not in the data.
MANE only needs GRCh38. MANE only keeps a variant with a MANE Select or MANE Plus Clinical transcript. VEP sets these flags on GRCh38 only, so on a GRCh37 or T2T family MANE only keeps nothing.

A search can stop part-way. Compound-het and recessive pairing and Expanded carrier screening read a limited number of candidates (up to 5,000) before they filter, ranked or not. When a search fills that window, a warning above the results says "Results may be incomplete" and after how many candidates the search stopped; the count is then a lower bound (for example 12+) and a match beyond the window is not shown. Narrow the filters with a region, a gene panel or a gene until the warning is gone.
A gene without Monarch data gets no phenotype credit and ranks lower; its Variant score is not affected. Look further down for strong variants, or untick Phenotype prioritization.
Without HPO terms on the affected members, the ranking uses the variant evidence only.

The ranking changes the order of a search, not what it finds. With an inheritance mode or Expanded carrier screening it ranks the same variants and compound-het pairs the search finds without it. A pair stays a pair, listed where its better-ranked variant ranks; each variant shows its own rank.
The score orders candidates within the family; it is not a probability of pathogenicity.

A warning that "Ranking may be incomplete" means more candidates matched than CoGA ranks at once (it says how many were ranked), so the best one may be missing: narrow the filters (a region, a panel, a gene, or a tighter frequency or impact).
Also hit by a structural variant

interpretation-and-review.title: Interpretation and review
interpretation-and-review.summary: Tag, annotate and classify variants — with the semi-automatic ACMG classifier — and keep the review state per family.
paragraphs: Record your interpretation as you go. Review state is kept per family: the same variant in two families has two separate records.

Each row or card has Review, Exclude and Report (one-click tags), Tags & notes and ACMG classify. An excluded variant stays in the list: its card folds to its heading and a bar marked Excluded, with Show card to unfold it and Undo exclude to take the tag off again; in the table view its row is dimmed.
ACMG classify opens a dialog that pre-evaluates the ACMG/AMP criteria from the variant, the gene and the family genotypes, and scores them on the ClinGen points scale.
A variant opened from the mtDNA analysis page gets a mitochondrial rule set.

The structural-variant page works the same way: Review, Exclude, Report, tags and notes, and ACMG (CNV) for the ClinGen copy-number classifier. Saving a CNV classification also freezes its evidence, so the report can tell whether it changed. An event called by more than one caller is listed once per caller, with one shared review: the classification freezes the evidence of the row you opened it from. Small-variant and SV review are counted separately on the family page.
blocks: Tags. The built-in tags are Review, Send for validation, Validated, Validation did not confirm, Confident AR single hit, Excluded and Report, the ACMG class tags, the VUS tiers and Secondary finding. An administrator can add custom tags for one project or for everyone. A renamed custom tag stays on every review that holds it. A deleted one stays too, marked (deleted): untick it to remove it from a review; it can no longer be added.
Notes keep your reasoning with the variant.
Report puts the variant in the family report.

Each criterion shows as checked (the data supports it), ● (consider), ✕ (the data argues against) or n/a (cannot apply). Hover it for the evidence; click to change it, and pick its strength. Only checked criteria count.
The bar at the top shows the points, the class and, for a VUS, the tier (Hot, Warm or Cold).
The header links to gnomAD, ClinVar, DECIPHER and a PubMed search on the gene and the patient's HPO terms.

Save classification stores the class as the variant's classification and review tag, together with every criterion and your note; the server recomputes the class. It also freezes the evidence — the ClinVar significance, the consequence and LoF call, the population frequencies, the in-silico scores and, for a missense variant, the gene's missense Z the dialog read — so the report can later tell whether it changed, and what.
Opening a classified variant again shows the criteria as you saved them.
Decision support, not an autoclassifier. The dialog pre-positions the criteria; you confirm them, adjust the strengths and add a note.
inline: ACMG classification reference (rules, points, mtDNA, CNV) →
furtherReading: In-depth referenceACMG classification reference (rules, points, mtDNA, CNV) →

clinical-report.title: Family report and sign-out
clinical-report.summary: Draft the family report from the tagged variants, see what changed, and sign the analysis out into a version that can never change. The clinical report is signed in the EPD.
paragraphs: Tag a variant with Report and it joins the family report (the Report button on the family page). The live report drafts readable text per reported variant — description, ACMG reasoning, gene context and phenotype overlap — and is where the analysis is signed out. Once it is signed out, the Report button opens its signed version.

Sign-out closes the analysis; the medical sign-off is in the EPD. Sign out report is the analyst's analytical sign-off: it closes the analysis and freezes it into a signed version. The clinical report is drafted and medically signed in the hospital's electronic patient record (EPD), not in CoGA, and refers to exactly one signed version: the one it rests on.

Sign out report is your analytical sign-off: it closes the analysis and freezes the reported result into a numbered version with a unique fingerprint, with what the analysis looked at: each reported variant's description as you reviewed it, the gene panels the family's searches applied, the reference-data releases, the repeat-expansion and Paraphase results (with each repeat count near a boundary marked, and whether QA had validated TRGT's counting units at each locus), what each coverage track held (read depth, a log2 ratio or unknown, and whether an upload or a package loaded it), in a PGT family each embryo's call at the region of interest as the family page shows it, with its phasing QC and that QC's verdict against the thresholds, and for a monogenic NIPT family its NIPT results (the NIPT page signs out through this same sign-out, see the NIPT chapter). The EPD refers to the signed version by its report code (for example 7KQM2X-2-4PHT). It stops for six things:

Your acknowledgement covers exactly what its dialog lists. If the concerns change before you click Sign out anyway, nothing is signed out: the dialog lists them as they are now, says the concerns changed, and asks for your reason again.

A PGT embryo call whose phasing QC does not meet its thresholds (⚠ phasing QC on the family page) does not stop the sign-out: the call stands, you decide on it, and the signed version records the warning.

A reason you give is frozen into the signed version and written to the audit trail. Signing out again creates a new version (Amend sign-out); earlier versions are never overwritten, and a clinical report that rests on the amended analysis refers to the new version. After signing out, the page shows the version you signed and its report code: quote that code in the EPD report. A mistyped code is refused as a typo, never taken for another record's. Report codes in the main menu finds the signed version a code names.

Only the signed version is. A signed case opens on its latest signed version, drawn from the frozen record: Signed version N — signed out by … on …, with its report code and fingerprint. It shows what was signed: each reported variant's description, classification, criteria, evidence and note, in a PGT family the embryo calls (PGT embryo results, with each call's QC verdict and the thresholds), in a monogenic NIPT family its NIPT results (NIPT results), the gene panels applied, the repeat expansions (each count near a boundary marked beside its call, ⚠ Near a boundary, and each locus's counting units as QA had recorded them) and Paraphase results, the coverage tracks (Coverage tracks: what each held, and from which file), the reference-data releases, and the checks at sign-out. It says what the record does not hold — the population frequencies and predictions, the gene and phenotype context, the audit trail — and never fills that in from current data. Print signed version N prints it, and Download signed version N (JSON) returns the record itself. Signed versions lists the earlier ones.

Open the live report shows the current data. It says This is the live report, not signed version N, and whether it still matches: amber when something changed since (it names what), grey when the check could not be made (treat it as unsigned). What version N does not hold could not be compared, and it names that too (Not in signed version N, so not compared: …). Its printout starts with Not the signed report.
blocks: Every reported variant, small variants and structural variants alike. If a list cannot hold them all, an Incomplete warning says so, on screen and in print, so a printout cannot pass for the whole list.

The repeat expansions and Paraphase findings marked Report: each with its gene and disease, every member's call with CoGA's status, your classification and note, and the marks differs from CoGA's status and Changed since review where they apply. Without any, the section says so.

A provenance footer with the CoGA version that produced the page, the in-house IVD statement and the manufacturer, and the versions behind the data: the pipeline tools, the assembly, the gene loci, the Monarch release and the HPO release. It prints with the report.

An evidence-drift banner when a classification's evidence changed after it was made: for example a new ClinVar significance, a new REVEL score or gnomAD frequency (REVEL 0.412 → 0.951), a new consequence or LoF call (LoF LC → HC), a new missense Z for a missense variant's gene, or a structural variant that now overlaps other genes. Re-review those variants.

The Clinical audit trail: who classified, tagged or annotated what, who reviewed a compound-heterozygous pair, who changed the pedigree or the family's phenotypes, and when. Entries can never be changed or deleted. It is for analysts and administrators: a reader of the family's project sees, on screen and in print, that it is not shown. It opens on the 200 most recent entries; when there are more, it says how many it shows, and Show older events loads the next 200. A printout that shows only part of the trail says so.
The Analysis pipeline settings recorded at import.

An Import incomplete warning at the top when a data import left the family partly loaded, or has not finished: it is still running, or it stopped part-way (for example the server restarted). It names the datasets that failed, or that the import had not finished, and the import job. A single upload that has not finished, or that failed and could not put back what it deleted, is named the same way, as a single-file upload, and so is a deletion of the family's data that has not finished (an administrator's deletion of a sample or of the family, a PED upload that replaces the family, a structure change that clears its data), as a deletion of this family's data. The same warning shows on every family page until an import, or an upload, has brought those datasets again.
An assembly outside the validated scope (the page says Not validated for clinical use): the report cannot be signed out.
Data being written: a data import of the family is queued or running, or an upload, or a deletion of its variants, is changing its data. Sign out once it has finished; there is no override.

Evidence drift, of a small variant, a structural variant or a CNV, including a reported variant that was never saved through ACMG classify or ACMG (CNV) (its evidence cannot be checked), and of a repeat or Paraphase review with a classification or the Report tag whose calls changed since: re-review, or acknowledge with a reason. The dialog lists each classification and what moved.

Sample QC that failed, or could not confirm the pedigree or a sample's identity, and for a NIPT family a NIPT quality check that failed: acknowledge with a reason. The dialog lists every concern before you write it, under its own heading: the checks that failed, the checks that could not run, the NIPT quality checks that failed, and the warnings, which do not stop the sign-out on their own. Each concern names the sample, the pair or the child it is about, and your reason covers all of them.

An incomplete import (the page says Import incomplete): import what failed again, or acknowledge with a reason. After an import that stopped part-way, re-run it with overwrite: an update skips data that is already there, partly written data too. After a failed overwrite that could not put the family's data back, import the whole family again with overwrite, every dataset the warning names and not only those that failed, and upload again with overwrite what an upload brought. After a single upload or a deletion that did not finish, upload or import again with overwrite what the warning names; after an administrator's deletion of a sample that did not finish, deleting the sample again also removes what the warning names of it.

Repeat and Paraphase calls without a review: a repeat call that reads Pathogenic, Premutation, Review or Not assessed, a count Near a boundary, or a Paraphase call that reads pathogenic, carrier or review, at a locus or region without a review (any tag, note or classification): review it, or acknowledge with a reason. A grey-zone call alone does not stop it.

Only people the laboratory authorises sign out. CoGA lets any analyst of the family's project press Sign out report, not a reader, and does not check that authority further. The laboratory decides who may sign out an analysis; CoGA records who did. The medical sign-off is given in the EPD.
inline: Sign-out closes the analysis; the medical sign-off is in the EPD.

Signed version N — signed out by … on …

specialised-analyses.title: Structural variants, repeats, Paraphase and mtDNA
specialised-analyses.summary: The analyses beyond small variants, including the CNV classifier and the variant summary.
paragraphs: The Structural variants page opens on the Mendeliome panel, with a population frequency below 1% and the affected members as carriers. Its filters are Phenotype, Inheritance and Support, Locations, Class and Breakpoints, Needlr Annotations and Review; the presets are Mendeliome, Dominant, Recessive-like and Any affected. Phenotype prioritization ranks SVs by the same phenotype score as small variants. Clear all filters removes the default.

A gene panel keeps an SV whose annotation names one of its genes or that overlaps one of its regions, whatever the panel's size, as on the small-variant page: the Mendeliome also keeps an SV in one of its genes whose annotation names that gene otherwise, and a small panel also keeps an SV whose annotation names one of its genes without overlapping it, such as a gene a few kilobases away. With a gene panel and a Gene symbol both filled in, an SV must meet both.

Min length and Exact length, under Class and Breakpoints, measure an SV by the Length the list shows, without the minus sign of a deletion: the caller's SVLEN; for a call written as its sequence without an SVLEN (as VCF 4.4 writes one), the bases it inserts or deletes; otherwise the end minus the start. An insertion is as long as the sequence it inserts, although most callers write its end at its start. A length typed with a minus sign, as the list writes a deletion's, is read without it. A translocation (BND, TRA) has no length: the list shows none, every minimum keeps it, and no exact length finds it.

A filtered search reads at most 50,000 SVs of the callset before it applies the filters, and with Phenotype prioritization on (the default) it ranks at most 5,000 of the SVs that match. When a search reaches either limit, a warning says "Results may be incomplete" ("Ranking may be incomplete" when the list is ranked), the count shows a +, and an SV beyond the limit is not shown: narrow the search with a region, a gene panel or a gene. A gene panel of any size, the Mendeliome included, and a gene are applied before the 50,000 are read, so the limit counts only the SVs they keep. The family report's list of reported SVs is not cut by this cap: it reads the reported SVs themselves, not the first 50,000.
ACMG (CNV) on a row opens the ClinGen copy-number classifier (Riggs et al. 2020): choose Copy-number loss or Copy-number gain, check the pre-selected criteria and add the rest.

Variant summary on the family page summarises the structural variants of every caller, HiFiCNV's copy-number calls included: counts per chromosome and type, sharing between members, and size distributions. The button appears when the family has structural variants. Small variants are not in it, nor are the WisecondorX and QDNAseq segments, which are coverage tracks rather than variants.
The Repeat expansions page lists each repeat locus with every member's call: the repeat count of each allele, and a status read against the locus's thresholds in the repeat catalogue (STRchive):

Aberrant only, ticked when the page opens, keeps every locus whose status is not Normal or Unknown, Not assessed included, and the page header counts the calls not assessed. The genome tracks colour each locus by the status its call was imported with, and keep it until the call is imported again; this page classifies every call again, against the catalogue as it is now.

Near a boundary. TRGT counts the motif across the region its own catalogue gives a locus, which need not be the clinical repeat number the locus's ranges count. At FMR1 it leaves out the AGG interruptions, so an allele reads 1 to 3 below its clinical number (a premutation of 55 repeats can read 53, in the grey zone); at HTT it also counts the CAG after the CAA interruption, one above the usual count; at POLG it counts four flanking GCT copies, so the common 10-repeat allele reads 14. Until QA and the laboratory director have validated a locus's counting units, a count within 3 repeats of a boundary the locus's classification uses is marked Near a boundary beside its call. Hover over or focus the mark for the count, the nearest count on each side that reads another status, and what is known of TRGT's count at the gene. The status itself is not changed: read the call with the mark in mind. Aberrant only keeps such a locus whatever its status, the page header counts the calls near a boundary, and a genome track says it in the locus's tooltip. An administrator records each locus's validation, with its reason, on the admin page Repeat catalogue; a validated locus is no longer marked. Signing out freezes the mark beside its call, and for each locus whether QA had validated its counting units, with the reason, by whom and when: a locus validated or withdrawn after sign-out makes the report say the repeat expansions changed since.

Some genes lie in regions with nearly identical copies, such as SMN1/SMN2 or PMS2, where standard variant calling fails. The Paraphase page shows, per locus, what Paraphase found there for each member: the copy number, and a status read from a catalogue of medical regions. Where the catalogue has a rule for the locus, the copy number reads as normal, carrier or pathogenic, or as review when it fits none of them; at a locus without a rule, a copy-number change or a fusion reads as review. A change is a copy number outside the normal range the catalogue records for the locus (6 for NEB, 4 for a gene with its pseudogene). On chrX a man has one copy and a woman two, by the sex Paraphase infers, else the pedigree's; without a sex a chrX value is not called normal. A field without a fixed normal value (highest_total_cn) and a no-call are no change. Copy-number changes and abnormal calls only, ticked when the page opens, shows the regions with such a change or with a member's call that reads Pathogenic, Carrier or Review: a fusion is reviewed without any change in copy number. Untick it to see every region.

Each repeat locus and Paraphase region has a review of its own, kept per family and reference assembly, and its card the controls of every variant card: Review, Exclude and Report toggle their tag, and Tags & notes opens the review. There you give your classification on the type's own scale, beside CoGA's status, which it never changes:

The ACMG class tags and VUS tiers are not offered here: they are the small variants' ACMG classes. A review that already holds one lists it, marked, so you can untick it. The card shows your classification as Review: …, and Differs from CoGA's status when it agrees with none of the members' calls (a Normal where every call reads Pathogenic, say): a review is of the locus or region, so a classification that fits one member's call is not marked. Exclude folds the card to its heading; it stays in the list, Aberrant only included.

A classification, and the Report tag, rest on the calls as they were when you saved them: CoGA freezes them. When the calls change after that (a new import, a locus whose counting units QA validated), the card says Changed since review, and the tooltip names what changed; No call since review when the family holds no call there any more. A save of tags or a note alone keeps the calls your classification rests on. Sign-out checks them again (see Clinical report).

Each sample's row in the family summary of the mtDNA analysis page gives its mean chrM depth and the share of chrM covered, and a QC status judged against the lab's limits (Sequencing QC thresholds). The depth comes from one coverage track that holds read depth: the sample's coverage BED when it was declared as read depth, otherwise HiFiCNV's depth where the import stored it as read. WisecondorX's and QDNAseq's bins, HiFiCNV's normalised depth and a coverage BED declared as a log2 ratio hold log2 ratios, not depths, and never count, nor does a coverage BED that does not say what it holds. A sample without a track of read depth shows the depth of its chrM calls, and the page's QC notes name each track left out and why.

Each mtDNA variant has the same review as a small variant, and its card the same controls: Review, Exclude and Report, Tags & notes and ACMG classify. It is one review: the same variant on the Small variants page shows the same tags and note, and Report puts it on the report with the other reported small variants. Exclude folds the card to its heading, as on the other variant pages. ACMG classify on a variant from the mtDNA analysis page uses the mitochondrial rule set.
blocks: Filter and review CNVs and other SVs with their genotypes, rank them by phenotype, classify copy-number changes, and tag them for the report.
Per-sample repeat calls, scored against the STRchive catalogue of disease loci.
Genes in paralogous or duplicated regions, where standard variant calling is unreliable.
mtDNA variants and large chrM deletions and duplications, each with its heteroplasmy per member, and each sample's mtDNA coverage.

Normal, Grey zone (the intermediate range), Premutation (an FMR1 allele of 55–200 repeats, which can expand in a child) and Pathogenic. Where the catalogue gives a locus a benign range and a pathogenic threshold but no grey zone, a count between the two reads Grey zone: it is neither benign nor pathogenic.
Review: outside catalogued ranges: a count the catalogue cannot classify at a locus that is pathogenic by contraction.
Review: two chrX alleles in a male: a male's call with two different chrX alleles, where he carries one; a note explains it.
The genome tracks colour each call by the status the repeat page gives it.

Not assessed: a call at a locus without thresholds. No catalogued locus matches its TRID (a locus the catalogue lacks, or a TRID spelled differently), or the catalogue gives the locus no threshold. CoGA cannot say whether such a count is normal; its cutoff reads No reference cutoff. Where the catalogue gives a locus a benign range but no threshold (STRchive's POLG: 10 repeats), a count inside the range reads Normal and any other count Not assessed; the cutoff reads normal 10 · no threshold. The count is the one TRGT reports for the catalogued motif across the whole locus, flanking copies included, so it can run higher than the count the range describes: in the TRGT catalogue in use (TRID CPEO_POLG), POLG's common allele of 10 repeats counts 14 and stays Not assessed.

A gene with several repeat tracts, each a locus of its own in STRchive (ARX, HOXA13), has thresholds per tract. A call whose TRID is the gene's name is read against the tract its region overlaps. If the region overlaps none of the tracts, or more than one, the call reads Not assessed, and its note names the tracts and says why.
Reviewing a repeat locus or a Paraphase region
a repeat locus: Pathogenic expansion, Reduced penetrance, Premutation, Intermediate (grey zone), Normal or Uncertain significance;
a Paraphase region: Affected, Carrier, Risk allele, Normal or Uncertain significance.

Copy-number changes and abnormal calls only

visualization.title: Genome visualisation
visualization.summary: From a candidate to its context: the genome and chromosome views, Circos and IGV, and how the small-variant and structural-variant tracks are drawn.
paragraphs: Tables are for finding candidates; viewers are for checking them in their genomic context. From the family page:
The IGV and View links on a variant row or card, and the Genome and Circos buttons above the structural-variant table, open in a new browser tab, so your filtered list stays as it was.
In the chromosome view each small variant is drawn by its class, with a legend on the track:

A variant with a conflicting or uncertain ClinVar record is drawn by its impact. A review tag draws a ring in the tag's colour around the mark; the mark itself does not change. Hover a mark for its impact, ClinVar status and parental origin.

When the sample shown has a parent in the family, the track has three rows: variants inherited from the father (top), from the mother (bottom), and of unknown origin (middle: homozygous, de novo or ambiguous). The origin comes from the parents' genotypes when both are there, otherwise from the phased genotype. Without a parent in the family there is one row.

Coverage is drawn one track per CNV caller, on the axis of what the track holds. The callers' log2 ratios share the log2-ratio axis, with the gain and loss colours and the caller's segments. Read depth is drawn on a depth axis from 0, without those colours or segments: a coverage BED declared as read depth, and a HiFiCNV depth file without autosomal depth, which gives no baseline to take a ratio against, so its depths are kept as read (the track's header says so). A coverage BED says what it holds when it is loaded; one that does not is drawn on its own range without an axis, and its header warns that it is read as neither depth nor a log2 ratio.

In a PGT family, judge each embryo's aneuploidy and large (>10 Mb) structural variants yourself, on its segment, copy-number (coverage) and APCAD tracks. CoGA shows the tracks but makes no aneuploidy call.
The PGT haplotype track is explained under Haplotype segregation.
The genome and chromosome views draw every SV that the structural-variant list shows, in one of six rows:

A CNV is placed by the copy number stored for the sample's call, as the SV ranking scores it: a male has one copy of chrX and chrY outside the pseudo-autosomal regions, and a CNV without a stored copy number counts as a loss. Hover an SV for its type as the caller wrote it, a CNV's copy-number change, and the call's copy number (CN). The Circos plot draws each SV the same way, from the calls of the whole family.
blocks: Genome view — chromosomes 1–22, X and Y with their variants and tracks. The mitochondrion, too small to see there, is in the chromosome view (chrM) and on the mtDNA analysis page.
Chromosome view — one chromosome with coverage, segments, APCAD, haplotypes and variant tracks. Clicking the ROI on the family page opens it here with 1 Mb on each side.
Circos plot — genome-wide structural relationships at a glance, drawn on chromosomes 1–22, X and Y of the family's assembly. For an assembly it cannot draw, the page says why and draws nothing.
IGV viewer — the reads at a locus, on the genome of the family's assembly. For an assembly it has no genome for, the page says so and opens none, rather than another assembly's genome.

Viewers show only what was imported. A coverage, segment, APCAD or haplotype track appears when that data was loaded for the sample, so an empty track usually means the layer is missing, not that the viewer failed. When a view holds too many variants to draw, the track says so: zoom in or filter.
Deletions of any subtype (DEL:ME), and CNVs that remove a copy
Duplications of any subtype (DUP:TANDEM), and CNVs that add a copy
Any other type, and CNVs that change no copy number, in grey
inline: Viewers show only what was imported.

haplotype-segregation.title: Haplotype segregation (PGT)
haplotype-segregation.summary: Follow the parental haplotypes through the family to see which embryos inherited the disease haplotype — and when not to trust the call.
paragraphs: The Haplotypes track (chromosome view and genome overview) is CoGA's PGT tool. It colours each person's two haplotypes by the parental homolog they descend from, finds the haplotype that carries the disease allele, and calls each embryo from it.

Each embryo's call is a badge in the Family members table on the family page: Affected / at risk, Carrier, Unaffected or Uninformative. A call that the embryo does not carry a disease haplotype needs the embryo's own haplotype, seen across the ROI; without it the embryo reads Uninformative. CoGA works the calls out on the server, from the stored haplotypes, and Sign out report freezes the same calls into the signed version (PGT embryo results), each with the haplotypes it rests on, its warnings, its QC at the ROI and that QC's verdict against the thresholds. Next to the badge may be:

Review ROI markers → shows the phased genotypes of every member across the ROI, with each child's Mendelian-error rate. Use it to re-check a surprising call: a single marker that disagrees with its neighbours is noise, not a crossover, and a clear Mendelian-error rate points to a swap or a wrong pedigree.
In a single-parent (donor) family the donor lane stays grey, and a recessive call is uninformative because the donor side is unknown.
blocks: Phased imputed genotypes (GLIMPSE2) for the couple, the embryos and the relatives you want coloured.
A correct pedigree, including the grandparents, who anchor the disease haplotype.

Every member's sex, recorded before the phased genotypes are imported. On chrX a man has one X outside the pseudo-autosomal regions, and the haplotypes there are built with the sexes recorded at the import: after recording or correcting a sex, import the phased genotypes again.
Affected and carrier status on the members that define the disease haplotype.

An inheritance model (if none is set, CoGA assumes recessive when a member is marked as a carrier, otherwise dominant) and a region of interest at the disease locus. Without an ROI there are no embryo calls.
P1 and P2 (blues) are the father's homologs, M1 and M2 (greens) the mother's. Untransmitted (grey) is a relative's homolog that was not passed down, or one CoGA could not place.

The disease haplotype has a line under the band: solid red (Affected) for a dominant or X-linked model, dashed orange (Carrier) for a recessive one. On the genome overview the line appears only on the ROI's chromosome.
The marker dots are the raw phased markers. Use them to check that a colour change is a real recombination and not phasing noise. On a very large region they are hidden: zoom in.

⚠ phasing QC — the embryo's phasing QC at the ROI does not meet its thresholds: at least 50 informative sites, a Mendelian error rate of at most 2%, and at least 6 markers on each parent's side the call reads. The tooltip names each measure, its value and its threshold. The call stands: check it in the ROI markers before you rely on it. These thresholds are provisional, to be confirmed by the laboratory director and QA. At an X-linked locus a man is counted with his one X: a son against his mother alone.
⚠ QC not counted — no phasing QC was counted at the ROI, so the call was not checked against the thresholds; the tooltip says why.
⚠ recombination — a haplotype change inside the ROI or within 250 kb of it; the call may not hold across the locus.

⚠ phase corrected — CoGA undid a phase switch in a parent's haplotypes inside or close to the ROI. Where the phase switched is known only roughly, so the call across the locus is less certain: review the ROI markers.
⚠ uninformative — no call is made: no disease haplotype could be resolved, or the embryo's haplotype does not cover the ROI.

⚠ sex unknown — an X-linked recessive call depends on the embryo's sex, which is not recorded. The embryo then reads Affected / at risk or Uninformative, and the warning gives the call for a son and for a daughter. Record the sex to resolve it.

monogenic-nipt.title: Monogenic NIPT
monogenic-nipt.summary: Screen a pregnancy for single-gene disorders from maternal-plasma cfDNA and a paternal sample: set it up, read the page, print the report.
paragraphs: Monogenic NIPT screens a pregnancy for single-gene disorders from cell-free DNA (cfDNA) in maternal plasma, with a sample from the father. The fetus is never sequenced: its genotype is inferred from the cfDNA allele fractions and the fetal fraction (FF), the share of the cfDNA that comes from the fetus.

In Family builder, tick Monogenic NIPT (cfDNA from maternal plasma). Add the father, the cfDNA sample as the mother (mark it cfDNA (maternal plasma)) and the fetus as the proband. A package import does the same when its manifest says analysis_type: monogenic_nipt. The family page then shows a Monogenic NIPT button.

The data is the NIPT-M pipeline's output: a single-sample VCF of the plasma and one of the father, with a per-target coverage table for each (coverage_<sample>.txt). The package import finds them by the sample names of the PED. One combined VCF with a father column and a cfDNA column works as well. The calls must carry FORMAT/AD.

The built-in presets De novo, Paternal, inherited and Recessive (both parents carrier) set a view with high or moderate impact and a gnomAD frequency of 1% or less (a ClinVar pathogenic record overrides the frequency). Pick a gene panel as well. The page opens on De novo; a link with its own filters, such as Back to NIPT, opens on those.

Report on the NIPT page opens a printable summary: the fetal fraction, the quality checks, the coverage of the targets in scope, and the classified variants grouped as De novo in fetus, Dominant, transmitted, Recessive / biallelic risk and Other categories. Its footer names when it was made and the CoGA version that made it. Its Scope names the panel and genes you selected; your other filters do not apply. It lists up to 500 variants. When there are more, it says how many it lists of how many and where the list stops, on screen and in print: narrow the scope with a panel or a gene. Print report prints it. An Import incomplete or Not validated for clinical use warning heads it, on screen and in print, whenever the family page would show one. The report is live, never the signed record: it says so beside the latest signed version, and every printout starts with Draft or Not the signed report.

Sign out NIPT analysis on the NIPT page is the analytical sign-off: it freezes the analysis into the family's signed record, which the EPD report refers to by its report code. It is the family's own sign-out, with the same checks and report code, so the family has one signed record whether you sign out here or from the family report. The record holds the NIPT results as CoGA computed them: the fetal fraction and the quality checks, the coverage, and each variant tagged report with its category, reads and probabilities. Tag the variants you report first. Show reported (N), under the sign-out status, lists them before you sign out: the variants tagged report, with every other filter cleared. A tagged variant the analysis does not classify (not in the family's NIPT data, on the assay's artifact list, or without a call in the plasma) is in no list: the page names it above the list with the reason, as the signed record does. Besides the Sample QC, a NIPT quality check that failed (no fetal-fraction estimate, fetal-sex signals that disagree, or male DNA as the maternal plasma) stops the sign-out until you record a reason. Afterwards the signed version opens, with its report code; the NIPT page then shows Amend sign-out and says whether the data still matches the signed version. A reader of the family's project cannot sign out, here or on the report: the button says why.
blocks: The header shows the fetal fraction, its 95% confidence interval and the number of sites it rests on, a Low-confidence FF chip when the estimate is weak, and the filter funnel (Total, Quality-filtered, Artifact-filtered, Analysed). As on every family page, it warns Import incomplete while a data import has left the family partly loaded or has not finished, and Not validated for clinical use for a family outside the validated scope.

Quality checks come first: the fetal fraction (with the per-site median and the de novo window), the fetal sex from the father's X alleles and from the chrY coverage, paternity, the maternal plasma sample, the coverage of the capture targets and why cfDNA calls failed the quality filter. A failed paternity check means another father or a sample mix-up: do not read the variants.

The filters are the small-variant page's Pathogenicity, Annotations, In Silico, Frequency, Locations and Exclude filters and its review tags (Review and curation: the tags, not the classification or saved notes), plus Maternal/fetal categories (tick any of the eight; each shows its count), a minimum classification confidence and an Inheritance view: De novo in the fetus: calls in the fetal window without a supported call in the father, triaged and ranked by score. List de novo candidates of priority picks high, high and medium, or every candidate. Paternal, inherited by the fetus and Maternal, inherited by the fetus: each parent's alleles with the probability that the fetus inherited them. Also list the alleles the fetus did not inherit adds the rest. Recessive: both parents carriers: the genes where both parents are heterozygous for an allele, in a table with the fetal risk per gene.

De novo in the fetus: calls in the fetal window without a supported call in the father, triaged and ranked by score. List de novo candidates of priority picks high, high and medium, or every candidate.

Paternal, inherited by the fetus and Maternal, inherited by the fetus: each parent's alleles with the probability that the fetus inherited them. Also list the alleles the fetus did not inherit adds the rest.
Recessive: both parents carriers: the genes where both parents are heterozygous for an allele, in a table with the fetal risk per gene.

Each variant carries its category, the plasma reads, the father's genotype, the probabilities that the fetus inherited the paternal or maternal allele or is homozygous, a de novo candidate's priority and any flags, next to the usual annotation, tags and ACMG classification.

On-target coverage, under the variants, gives the median depth over the capture targets of the panel and genes you selected (every target without a selection) and how many genes have a weak target: a mean below 300× or a base without coverage, where a fetal variant can be missed. Coverage details opens the coverage page: the genes below target and above it, each opening to its targets and their depth. Back to NIPT returns to the NIPT page with your filters.

Read the probabilities, not only the category. A de novo or paternal allele shows clearly at any fetal fraction. Whether the fetus inherited a maternal allele needs depth and a fair fetal fraction: check its probability. The recessive risk assumes both alleles are pathogenic and, at two sites, in trans; an allele without a population frequency (every MNV) is noted.

Screening, not diagnosis. A NIPT call must be confirmed by an invasive diagnostic test. Check the fetal fraction and the quality checks before you read any variant, and a de novo candidate's absence in the father and its reads before you act on it.

explorers.title: Gene, variant and CNV explorers
explorers.summary: Questions beyond one case: a gene profile, a variant across the cohort, and the catalogue of clinical CNVs.
paragraphs: Three explorers answer questions beyond a single case. Open them from the menu under the arrow at the right of the top bar, or from the dashboard.

A profile per gene: the transcripts, badged MANE Select, MANE Plus Clinical, RefSeq Select and Ensembl Canonical; constraint metrics (pLI, LOEUF, missense constraint); disease associations with ClinGen and GenCC evidence and OMIM links; the Monarch gene–disease associations (see Phenotypes, panels and phenotype matching); and links to the main external resources.
Every small variant across the projects you can access, one row per variant: gene, variant, classification, consequence and tags, with the number of carriers (het and hom) and of families.
The catalogue of known clinical CNVs (syndromes and recurrent regions) for an assembly. Search by name, chromosome or type; each row shows the CNV, cytoband, location, size and ClinVar P/LP.
blocks: ACMG secondary finding says whether the gene is on the ACMG secondary-findings list that CoGA ships: On ACMG SF v3.3, with the phenotype, category, inheritance and variants to report the list gives the gene and its footnotes for it, or Not on ACMG SF v3.3. Not checked means the list was not read for this gene: its gene information was refreshed before CoGA had the list, or the list could not be read.

ClinGen dosage curation gives ClinGen's haploinsufficiency and triplosensitivity curations of the gene, the date of the curation and a link to ClinGen's report. The item with an HI score is ClinGen's haploinsufficiency score as dbNSFP carries it.
Filter as on the family page (gene, consequence, ClinVar, frequency, in-silico scores), plus tags and classification — for example every variant tagged Report.

The annotation filters work as on the family page: they must all hold on one transcript of the variant, one of the in-silico predictors you set is enough, and MANE only keeps nothing on GRCh37 or T2T (see Small-variant prioritisation).

A gene panel works as on the family page too: it keeps the variants of its genes and the variants in its regions (PanelApp's regions for the assembly, and each gene's position in the gene reference), so a variant whose annotation names its gene differently is kept. This holds for a panel of any size, the Mendeliome included.
Click a het, hom or family count to see the carriers per family, with links to their family pages.
Imputed calls are left out unless you tick Include imputed variants (GLIMPSE2 / SHAPEIT).

Download CSV exports the filtered variants with their annotation, up to 50,000 rows. A file that misses matches has TRUNCATED in its name, and the page says why: more variants matched than the 50,000 rows (narrow the filters), or the tag or classification filter matched more than the 200,000 variants one search takes (filter on fewer tags or classifications).

ClinVar P/LP, for example 12 loss · 3 gain, counts the pathogenic or likely pathogenic ClinVar copy-number variants that overlap the region by at least 30% both ways, as counted when the knowledgebase was built.
"—" means that the knowledgebase was built without ClinVar: not recorded, not zero.
Click a CNV for its detail page, with its description, the supporting ClinVar records and links to OMIM and DECIPHER. The same page opens when you click a clinical CNV in the viewers.
Counts follow your access. The variant explorer counts only the projects you can see, so its cohort counts reflect your accessible cohort.

administration.title: Administration
administration.summary: The admin dashboard: reference data, users and access, data management, variant configuration, database operations and audit logs.
paragraphs: Administrator tools sit behind admin access. Admin, in the top-bar menu or on the dashboard, opens the admin dashboard, grouped in six areas.
blocks: Species & assemblies — the genome builds and their reference data (cytobands, genes, clinical CNVs, segmental duplications, DGV), with each dataset's status. Refresh the human gene information, rebuild the clinical-CNV knowledgebase, or upload a reference file.
Gene panels — the panel catalogue: create panels, import them from PanelApp, and see their genes.

HPO terminology — the HPO release in use and the SHA-256 of the file it came from; preview and apply a new release. The release is the one the file states; a file that states another than the expected release you enter, or none, is refused.

Monarch data — load the Monarch release (gene–disease and disease–phenotype links) that powers phenotype matching and the ranking. Load it once after installation and about monthly; loading it also rebuilds the Mendeliome panel.

Repeat catalogue — for each repeat locus, whether QA has validated that TRGT's count there is the clinical repeat number, with the reason, who and when, and the history of these records. Until a locus is validated, the repeat page marks its counts near a boundary (Structural variants, repeats, Paraphase and mtDNA). Each record needs a reason and is kept in the clinical audit trail. Record a locus as validated only when TRGT's count there is the clinical repeat number: a locus whose count needs a correction stays not validated, as CoGA applies no correction yet. The loci the stored calls name are listed first.

Users — accounts, how each signs in (Microsoft or a password), roles and activation, and each user's projects with their level there (analyst or reader). A colleague's first Microsoft sign-in makes their account, a viewer in no project. Set an account's role in its Role list (CoGA asks you to confirm; you cannot change your own). Activate a new account here; deactivate one to revoke access without deleting its history (not your own: another administrator does that). An import, a gene reference sync or a clinical CNV knowledgebase rebuild the account asked for that has not started yet is then not run, and a rebuild not yet loaded loads nothing: its job ends failed, saying why. The same holds once you set an administrator's role to viewer.

Projects & access — the projects (each tied to an assembly) and which families, samples and users belong to them. A user sees only the data of their projects, and the cohort counts in the explorers follow the same scope. Tick a user to make them a member and choose their level next to their name: an analyst reads and changes the project's records; a reader (a student, say) reads, searches, exports and prints them and saves their own filter presets, but changes nothing and does not see the audit trail. A member added starts as an analyst. Administrators have every right in every project. A case can be assigned to, or reviewed by, an analyst of its projects or an administrator: one assigned to someone you make a reader keeps them, marked (not eligible), until it is changed.

Family & sample data — the inventory of families and samples: open a family's members and data, change its projects, download and verify the original import files, or delete a data layer, a sample or a family (this cannot be undone and is recorded in the audit log; deleting a sample or a family is also written to the family's Clinical audit trail, a family's deletion as its last entry). Deleting a family asks for its name, typed out, and the reason it goes, which its last entry records; without a reason it is not deleted. Deleting a sample takes out only its own calls: the other members' small variants stay as they were, in every callset. A file kept in a storage bucket is not downloaded here; Verify checks it against the bucket's record of it instead of its SHA-256. A file recorded outside the import folders (FAMILY_IMPORT_ROOTS, a bucket's among them) and CoGA's upload folder is marked as not read, and is neither downloaded nor verified; a refused Verify says why. Deleting a sample or a family deletes CoGA's own copies of its uploaded files, never a package's files.
Family statuses — the workflow statuses analysts give a case.

Sequencing QC thresholds — the warning and error cut-offs per assay behind the Seq. QC chip. None ship by default; a metric without a cut-off reads as not assessed, and a sample with no cut-off for any of its metrics shows Not run on the chip.
Package import — import a family package (see Case setup and data import).

Variant tags — create, rename, recolour or remove custom review tags, for one project or for everyone. A renamed tag stays on every review and saved filter that uses it; a removed tag stays on the reviews that hold it, marked deleted, and can no longer be added. The built-in and ACMG tags are listed for reference.
Preset filters — the catalogue of the small-variant presets the team uses. Presets are saved on the small-variant page.

ClickHouse tables & operations — technical database maintenance, for the bioinformatics team. Each assembly shows the last result of the scheduled integrity check and when it ran; Integrity check runs one now.

Audit logs — every request to the server (who, what, when, the outcome) and every button and link a user clicked. Identifiers are masked, so the log shows how CoGA is used without exposing patient data. The Flags column marks a request for a family, sample or project outside the user's projects, which CoGA answered as for an unknown one, a row in which a value the database cannot store was saved as an escape, naming the columns, an account made at its first Microsoft sign-in or whose role or activation changed (from and to), and every request of the emergency administrator's password sign-in (Emergency sign-in). It is separate from each family's Clinical audit trail on the report.

glossary.title: Glossary
glossary.summary: Short definitions of the terms used in CoGA.
blocks: ACMG class — the five-tier variant classification: benign, likely benign, VUS, likely pathogenic, pathogenic.
Affected versus carrier — affected status describes the person, carrier status the genotype. They are recorded separately: an unaffected person can be a carrier.
Analyst / reader — a member's level in a project. An analyst reads and changes the project's records; a reader only reads them. An administrator has every right in every project.

APCAD — What the abbreviation stands for is to be filled in by the laboratory. A sample's track of allele fractions at single-nucleotide sites. For an embryo, read from the PGT pipeline's VCF, each point is the share of the embryo's reads that carry the alternate allele (0 to 1) at a site where only one parent carries that allele, drawn in that parent's colour; where the run wrote PCF segments, each parent's are drawn over the points. From HiFiCNV the track holds the folded minor allele fraction instead (0 to 0.5), with no parent of origin. It is one of the tracks on which the analyst judges an embryo's aneuploidy and large structural variants; CoGA makes no call from it.
Assembly — the reference genome build (for example GRCh38) a project uses.
cfDNA — cell-free DNA. In NIPT: the DNA in maternal plasma, mostly maternal with a small fetal part.
ClinVar — the public archive of variant–condition interpretations.
CNV / SV — a copy-number variant is a deletion or duplication; a structural variant is any larger rearrangement, including CNVs, insertions, inversions and translocations.
Compound heterozygous — two different variants in one gene, one on each copy (in trans).
De novo — present in a child and absent in both parents. On a son's X or Y outside the pseudo-autosomal regions, only the mother (X) or the father (Y) passes that chromosome on.
Embryo call — CoGA's derived PGT result for an embryo at the ROI: affected / at risk, carrier, unaffected or uninformative.
EPD — the hospital's electronic patient record. The clinical report is drafted and medically signed there, not in CoGA, and refers to one signed version of the analysis.
Fetal fraction (FF) — the share of the cfDNA that comes from the fetus.
Haplotype, homolog — a homolog is one of a person's two copies of a chromosome; a haplotype is the set of alleles on one homolog.
Heteroplasmy — the fraction of mitochondrial genomes that carry a variant.
HPO — the Human Phenotype Ontology: a hierarchy of clinical phenotype terms, from general to specific.
IBD — identity by descent: a stretch of DNA that two relatives inherited from the same ancestor.
IBS0 — the share of sites where two samples have opposite homozygous genotypes; near zero for a parent and child.
In-silico predictors — CADD, REVEL, SpliceAI, SIFT, PolyPhen and AlphaMissense: scores that predict a variant's effect or splice impact.
Kinship (φ) — a measure of relatedness: about 0.25 for parent and child or siblings, 0.125 for second-degree relatives.
LoF — loss of function: a variant predicted to abolish the gene product (stop gained, frameshift, canonical splice site).
MANE Select / MANE Plus Clinical — agreed reference transcripts for clinical reporting; RefSeq Select and Ensembl Canonical are each database's representative transcript.
Mendelian error — a child's genotype that cannot come from its parents' genotypes; many of them point to a sample swap or a wrong pedigree.
Mendeliome — CoGA's built-in panel of every gene that Monarch says causes a disease or is associated with one; the default scope of the variant pages.
MNV — multi-nucleotide variant: neighbouring bases changed together.
Monarch Initiative — a knowledge graph that links genes, diseases and HPO phenotypes.
NeedLR — the structural-variant annotation tool of the long-read pipeline; its annotations fill the Needlr Annotations filters.
P / LP / B / LB — pathogenic, likely pathogenic, benign, likely benign.
Paraphase — a caller for genes in paralogous or duplicated regions.
PGT — preimplantation genetic testing: testing embryos before transfer.
Phenotype similarity — a score for how well two sets of HPO terms match, weighting rare, specific terms more heavily.
pLI / LOEUF — gene constraint: how intolerant a gene is to loss of function (a high pLI or a low LOEUF means constrained).
popmax — the highest allele frequency in any gnomAD sub-population.
Priority score — the Exomiser-style score that ranks candidates within a family; not a probability.
Recombination — a crossover between the two homologs at meiosis; the haplotype an embryo carries changes at that point.
ROI — region of interest: the gene or locus a family is about.

Sign-out — the analyst's analytical sign-off in CoGA: it closes the analysis and freezes it into a signed version that can never change. The medical sign-off is given on the clinical report, in the EPD.
Trans / cis — two variants on opposite homologs (trans) or on the same homolog (cis).
TRGT — tandem-repeat genotyping, used for repeat-expansion calls.
VAF — variant allele fraction: the share of reads that carry the alternate allele.
VUS tier (hot / warm / cold) — a split of the VUS band by ACMG points: hot 4–5, warm 2–3, cold 0–1.
